modern: Constantly consider how all things, such as they are now, were the same in time past too; and consider that they will be the same again. And place before your eyes entire dramas and stages of the same form, whatever you have learned from your own experience or from older history; for example, the whole court of Hadrianus, and the whole court of Antoninus, and the whole court of Philippus, Alexander, Croesus; for all those were dramas such as we see now, only with different actors.

explained.summary: History keeps repeating with a new cast. Picture entire royal courts from the past: Hadrian’s, that of Antoninus Pius (Marcus’s adoptive father), and those of Philip of Macedon, Alexander the Great and Croesus, the famously rich king of Lydia. They were all the same play we watch now, only with different actors. Seeing this takes the novelty and the melodrama out of the present.
explained.today: The office reshuffle, the family feud, the gossip about who’s in and who’s out: someone has played every one of these scenes before. Recognising the script makes it easier not to get swept up in it.
